series.title: Unemployment
series.definition: Unemployment refers to the share of the labor force that is without work but available for and seeking employment.
series.originating_source: ILO Modelled Estimates database (ILOEST), International Labour Organization (ILO), uri: https://ilostat.ilo.org/data/bulk/, publisher: ILOSTAT, type: external database, date accessed: January 17, 2026
series.revision_note: One current WDI vintage across all years. Historical values may be revised. Do not splice with older vintages; see the source definition for method changes.

series.note: Youth unemployment refers to the share of the labor force ages 15-24 without work but available for and seeking employment. One current WDI vintage across all years. Historical values may be revised. Do not splice with older vintages; see the source definition for method changes.

series.title: Labour force participation
series.definition: Labor force participation rate is the proportion of the population ages 15 and older that is economically active: all people who supply labor for the production of goods and services during a specified period.

series.note: Labor force participation rate is the proportion of the population ages 15 and older that is economically active: all people who supply labor for the production of goods and services during a specified period. One current WDI vintage across all years. Historical values may be revised. Do not splice with older vintages; see the source definition for method changes.

series.title: GDP growth
series.definition: Gross domestic product is the total income earned through the production of goods and services in an economic territory during an accounting period. It can be measured in three different ways: using either the expenditure approach, the income approach, or the production approach. This indicator denotes the percentage change over each previous year of the constant price (base year 2015) series in United States dollars.
series.revision_note: One current WDI vintage across all years. Historical values may be revised. Do not splice with older vintages; see the source definition for method changes.

series.title: GDP per capita
series.definition: Gross domestic product is the total income earned through the production of goods and services in an economic territory during an accounting period. It can be measured in three different ways: using either the expenditure approach, the income approach, or the production approach. The core indicator has been divided by the general population to achieve a per capita estimate.This indicator is expressed in current prices, meaning no adjustment has been made to account for price changes over time. This indicator is expressed in United States dollars.

series.title: Consumer price inflation
series.definition: Inflation as measured by the consumer price index reflects the annual percentage change in the cost to the average consumer of acquiring a basket of goods and services that may be fixed or changed at specified intervals, such as yearly.

series.title: Manufacturing value added
series.definition: Manufacturing includes industries classified in ISIC (Rev. 3) major division C and is defined as the physical or chemical transformation of materials or components into new products. Value added is the contribution to the economy by a producer or an industry or an institutional sector, which is estimated by the total value of output produced and deducting the total value of intermediate consumption of goods and services used to produce that output. This indicator is expressed as a percentage of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) which is the total income earned through the production of goods and services in an economic territory during an accounting period.

series.title: Labour productivity
series.definition: GDP per person employed is gross domestic product (GDP) divided by total employment in the economy. Purchasing power parity (PPP) GDP is GDP converted to 2021 constant international dollars using PPP rates. An international dollar has the same purchasing power over GDP that a U.S. dollar has in the United States.
